slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A figure has rotational symmetry if a rotation of more than 0 and less than 360 degrees about its center maps it onto itself. The smallest such angle for a regular n-gon is 360/n degrees.

Point symmetry is rotational symmetry of 180 degrees: every point P has a partner P' with the center as the midpoint of PP'. A parallelogram has point symmetry. An equilateral triangle has rotational symmetry (120 degrees) but not point symmetry.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: What is the smallest rotation that maps a regular hexagon onto itself? Does it have point symmetry?
slides.reveal: 60 degrees; yes, because 180 is a multiple of 60.
